newsitem.title: USA: SEC, U.S. attorney subpoena Dade Cty bond records.
newsitem.headline: SEC, U.S. attorney subpoena Dade Cty bond records.

text.p: Dade County Commissioner James Burke, who has been linked in Miami Herald reports to an alleged bond kickback scheme, said on Friday that federal investigators have subpoenaed all county records of bond deals in which Burke expressed an interest.

"They've subpoenaed documents from the finance department and I've encouraged them (department staff) to send more than they subpoenaed because I want to get the full story of what happened," Burke said.
Both the U.S. Attorney's Office and the Securities and Exchange Commission subpoenaed the records, Burke told Reuters.
Neither the U.S. Attorney's office nor the SEC would comment on the probe.
However, since Burke was chairman of the finance committee that oversees county bond issues, the subpoena could apply to just about any county bond issue, he said.
He described the subpoenae as "further fishing."
Burke, who is black, said he believes investigators are probing "primarily the minority transactions and black firms" because he has been an advocate for including minority-owned firms in bond deals.
"I've said from the rostrum that things are not going to be fair until you have inclusion of black firms, particularly at the senior level," Burke said.

The Miami Herald said FBI videotapes show Calvin Grigsby, the former president of the California firm Grigsby Brandford & Co, allegedly offering Burke a $300,000 kickback in exchange for steering bond business to the firm.
The conversation allegedly took place last month in a San Francisco hotel where Burke, Grigsby and Miami municipal bond firm owner Howard Gary discussed the kickbacks, the newspaper said.
Burke vehemently denied wrongdoing.

"There has been no bribery," Burke said. "One of the things that will become clear is that under our rules and procedures we have in place, the kind of one-person manipulation that has been alleged cannot happen."
Burke said he has seen the videotape and that it depicts a conversation manipulated by a government informant.

Burke did not identify the informant but the Miami Herald has reported that Gary was cooperating with investigators and secretly recorded conversations implicating Grigsby and Burke in bribery and kickbacks.
"They made it sound like a locked case. If it was a locked case, they would have gone out and indicted," Burke said.
He said neither he nor his lawyer had been advised of any time frame for possible arrests.

"The government has an informant ...that they sent fishing and most of the tapes and videos they have are going to show the informant doing pretty much most of the talking and orchestrating, and will not show any activity by other people, particularly by me, other than talking and responding to them more as a friend," Burke said.
An official at Howard Gary & Co said Gary had no comment, and the FBI also declined to comment.
No charges have been filed in connection with the Dade bond allegations.

Burke said that allegations have been made in press reports that he is steered to Grigsby Brandford, a $183 million revenue bond refunding for a recyling plant, the firm was selected as senior manager by the plant owner, in response to an unsolicited proposal from Grigsby Brandford.
Other Dade County finance officials have also said the underwriter was selected by reclying plant officials, and not by the county.

The other deal linked to the allegations, a tentative $165 million revenue bond issue for a new basketball arena, was awarded to Grigsby Brandford because they were next in line among the county's standing pool of bond underwriters, Burke said.
"It was part of our regular rotation," he said.
Burke said that during earlier phases of the investigation, federal investigators had made broad inquiries about county finance officials.
"They were asking about other commissioners, administrators. (the Federal inquiries) were in fact general, it was not any particular transaction or set of transactions," he said.

Burke and the county elections supervisor said investigators had not subpoenaed any Burke campaign records, although the elections official said those records could be easily reviewed without a subpoenae.
